steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Spray a baking sheet with nonstick spray.
Arrange eggplant rounds on the prepared baking sheet and sprinkle with 1/2 of the Parmesan. Layer one tomato slice over each eggplant round, then sprinkle with remaining Parmesan.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Eggplant Tomato Bake
raw_recipe.description: Like tomatoes and eggplants? Then you'll love this recipe that pairs them with fat-free Parmesan. Each bite is savory, cheesy goodness, with no guilt!
raw_recipe.name: Eggplant Tomato Bake

review.reviewBody:
Simple, light, quick, and really quite good. After a couple of bites we declared this dish an everyday keeper. It even looks attractive on the plate.

I do think the recipe is improved by taking a moment to add a little seasoning. Here are the details of what I did:

Instead of using a greased cookie sheet, I used parchment paper. 

Before cooking, using a paint brush, I brushed each side of the eggplant slices with olive oil to coat the entire surface and then seasoned well with salt and black pepper on both sides. Then I sprinkled on some dried basil (had no fresh basil on hand). Topped this with the tomato slice and then topped that with FRESH grated parmesan cheese. 400 degrees for about 20 minutes did the trick; timing was not too critical.

I salted the eggplant rounds and let them sweat for 30 minutes and rinsed. That is key to removing bitterness and honestly I think it helps the mush factor. Otherwise I made these exactly as written with a hint of garlic salt and it was amazing. I baked for 15 minutes and these weren't mushy at all but still tender enough to eat. All of my ingredients were from my garden. Even those around the house who don't like Eggplant liked it this way. Thanks for sharing.

There is no way to go wrong with this. We like eggplant very tender. I baked it at 375 for about 45 minutes and then added pesto to some slices and marinara to others and topped with sliced roma tomato and a bit of mozarella and baked a bit longer. YUM!! Also some I dipped in egg wash and then panko and it was absolutely WONDERFUL! It is also good topped with spinach or basil or anything like a little pizza!

So the recipe can be kept just as it is or played with cause it is so very very fun! And so much better than a soggy mess that my eggplant often comes out when I fry it and salt it and make it weep. This texture is perfect. I just need a bushel of eggplants now!

It's cheap, it's easy, it's nutritious. The taste is not great, but I think it just needs some spices and it'll be good. Unlike most reviewers, I prefer it if my eggplant is NOT moist, so I sliced it and sprinkled it with salt earlier in the day so it'd dry out a little bit. The tomatoes and cheese provided plenty of moisture without adding any to the eggplant.
I sprinkled the eggplant with onion salt, black pepper, and some parsley before adding the tomato and cheese and I liked this a lot better on my 2nd try.

This was really delicious. I did however, make a few minor adjustments after reading some reviews & for my own personal preference. I took the skin off of the eggplant and brushed on a little olive oil, sprinkled the eggplant with salt, pepper, and basil. Sprinkled with Parmesan cheese. Top with tomato and seasoned with pepper, salt, and basil and topped with mozzarella cheese. I baked for 25 minutes and served over pasta. It came out wonderful. My husband, mother-in-law, 6 yr. old step daughter, and 18 month old daughter, and I LOVED it! It will absolutely be making it again! Thank you for this excellent recipe :)

Deliciously awesome! If you like eggplant, you'll love this dish. I made just a few changes - I very lightly brushed all sides and edges of eggplant slices (except the top) with olive oil, then lightly brushed a very thin layer of pesto (cuz I had it in my fridge) on the top, then added a bit of salt, pepper and dried basil on top of that before adding the tomato slice. I sprinkled more salt/pepper/basil on the tomato then put some mozzarella on that. I baked it for about 20 minutes and it turned out oh so good!

I made it tonight for a snack and we loved it. I made some changes to it. I sliced it in rather thin slices coated both sides with evoo, then seasoned with garlic salt, lightly coated with panko bread crumbs and parmesan, added sliced tomato, then covered with asiago and English country cheddar cheese mixed with parmesan. I baked it approx. 20 minutes and it came out delicious. I would make more changes next time by adding marinara sauce, basil, which I forgot to add, and thicker slices of tomato. I never peel eggplant but I will for this recipe, it was difficult to slice after it was baked. Easy to make and plan to do again as we are big on eggplant!

I've made this multiple times. BF loves it. I salt the eggplant slices for 20-30 minutes to bring out the moisture and improve the cooked texture. Sometimes I add basil pesto between the tomato and cheese.

Fast, easy, low calorie, and flavorful. I used organic Japanese eggplant; I did not peel it. I layered the eggplant with organic Roma tomato slices and minced basil; seasoned with salt and pepper. You could also use minced garlic, garlic powder, or onion powder.

Super Super Easy!! I peeled the eggplant, glazed with olive oil then put a little cheese on top of the eggplant. Then I put sliced tomato with italian seasoning, salt, pepper, and a little more cheese. Delish! And it only took about 20 min to bake. Oh, I broiled at the end for a couple mins.

Loved it .... after adding salt and pepper, pesto, and EVOO. Even though this added calories, it is still next-to-nothing calories. YUM. I think it's more like an appetizer. I left on the eggplant skin and baked at 400 degrees for 20 minutes was nice.
Easy but I hate smell n taste of parm so used mozzarella n cheddder cheese instead
I would make this again, but next time I'll cook the eggplant first for a bit, and then put the cheese and tomato on. The eggplant wasn't cooked. Still tasted pretty good though.

Easy and tasty..I did as some other reviewers suggested added seasoning..Italian seasoning , crushed red pepper, salt, black pepper..also I did not have a large tomato..so I used cherry tomato’s that I sliced and topped each slice of egg plant.
Really easy to do and really tasty! Loved it!
Loved this. So simple and delicious. I just added a little black pepper to the parmesan. Glad I did.
It was really good. I did add some garlic just to add a little bit of flavor. The only thing I would change is adding some more seasoning on it to make it a little more flavorful.

It's cheap, it's easy, it's nutritious. The taste is not great, but I think it just needs some spices and it'll be good. Unlike most reviewers, I prefer it if my eggplant is NOT moist, so I sliced it and sprinkled it with salt earlier in the day so it'd dry out a little bit. The tomatoes and cheese provided plenty of moisture without adding any to the eggplant.
I sprinkled the eggplant with onion salt, black pepper, and some parsley before adding the tomato and cheese and I liked this a lot better on my 2nd try.
Excellent recipe only change I made was using parchment paper and adding fresh ground pepper to eggplant and tomato
You can make all kinds of tasty changes and as long as I have tomatoes in season...I could eat it everyday!
